newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. to investigate alleged attacks in Angola.
newsitem.headline: U.N. to investigate alleged attacks in Angola.

text.p: The U.N. Observer Mission in Angola is attempting to verify government claims of an attack on two towns in the country's northeast by troops of the former rebel movement UNITA, a U.N. official said on Wednesday.
"We have received these reports from the government," the U.N. official said. "We are sending a team to the area to try to verify these claims now."
Angolan National Radio reported on Tuesday that UNITA had attacked the towns of Maquesse and Caxinagagi in Lunda Norte Province. It gave no estimates of casualties.

Both towns were taken from UNITA during an army offensive into the diamond-rich zone during May and June. In past weeks UNITA has succeeded in recapturing a few of the towns it lost to the government.
UNITA and the government fought a two-decades civil war that ended with a peace treaty in 1994.

Although UNITA entered into a power-sharing agreement with the government in April and over 60 of its members joined the country's National Assembly, the former rebels continue to hold vast areas of the countryside and have been accused by the government and others of maintaining an army of thousands.
